title: Willie Hightower: John Lindsay and his band
summary: Hightower describes John Lindsay, a bass player pressed into playing trombone in his band and on his records, and the band's men like Fred Palm.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: You were talking about John Lindsay when he played bass?
Yeah, well you see, when he went to the Army he was a bass player.
So they carried a box around? Huh? They carried a box around?

Yeah, well that was in the Army. His daddy was a violin player. His brother's here now. Oh, his brother's still here? Yeah, his brother's here. He's a violin player. Joe Lindsay. Joe Lindsay's name. Where does he live in? Somewhere on the Prairie. Yeah, 40th around there. 40th to Prairie. Somewhere around. John Lindsay's, Joe Lindsay.
Joe was the one that's living.
That's living, yeah, John's dead. And when he came back he left here and went with the 8th Regiment band to the Army. And when he came back, he came back and Sergeant Tucker had the band.
He was a good trombone player then.

He was the 8th number one trombone player. But if he could get out of playing trombone he wouldn't play. If he wanted to play a job now he wouldn't play bass. He always wanted to play bass. But I made him play trombone.
He was on the records then too then? Yeah.

And you played trombone on the records? Yeah. He played trombone on all of my records that I made. Because that's the only way, if you wanted a man out of my band, at them times that's the only way you could get him, is to hire him or to hire me. Or get permission from me because he wouldn't play with you. See John was, the whole time, up until I lost my home, he lived with us. Him and his wife lived with us. Oh, he did? Yes. We lived together after we come up here. And the clarinet player was a male carrier. And he didn't depend on music for a living. What was his name again? Fred Palm. Fred Palm. E. E. Flat, saxophone player. And he'd tell you, he'd say, if you want me to play a gig with you at night, you'd call Willie up. Well, they'd say, I can go, I can go. And you'd have to call me, then I'd call Fred and tell Fred to go where he wanted. And I had another man from New Orleans, that probably, I don't know if you know, that I used in the band here. His name was, what's the drummer's name?
